    Deep ray paths and endpoint socles #

    Relate the source's ray-level notion of a deep path to the ordinary endpoint bimodule socle after singular paths have been normalized. This supplies the scalar-proportionality half of the semi-normalized presentation on every deep ray contour.

    source
    def LargeIndecomposable.SplitBasicIdempotents.IsBGRSDeepRayPath {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [HasBGRSPairDichotomy S.ProjectiveCategory] {i j : RayVertex S.RayCategory} (p : Quiver.Path i j) :
    Prop

    A ray path is deep when multiplication by every endpoint-radical ray vanishes on the appropriate side.

      Conversely, a nonzero ray path whose lifted ordinary composite lies in the endpoint bimodule socle is ray-deep. Ordinary endpoint annihilation passes to the ray category because a zero ordinary product is a BGRS special pair, whose ray product is zero.
